Definition: from a compound of G2087 and G2218; to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly:--unequally yoke together with.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, heterozygéō means unequally yoke together with. It occurs just once, in 2 Corinthians.
TheologicalSignificance: I take heterozygéō as it stands — unequally yoke together with — and read the passage with that plain sense in mind.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
